title: Existence of a hexatic phase for two-dimensional Riesz gases
reason: The primary source supplies a qualitative phase-diagram expectation, not a fully quantified theorem or fixed microscopic correlation observable. STATEMENT.md distinguishes recovered model assumptions from a proposed formalization.

primary_source.author: Mathieu Lewin
primary_source.title: Coulomb and Riesz gases: The known and the unknown
primary_source.location: Section VI.2 (ledger calls it VI.B, PDF pages 66-67); HTML lines 1688-1692
primary_source.short_quote: fast decay of translational correlations and slow decay of (six-fold) orientational correlations
primary_source.model: Classical d=2 Riesz gas; V_0=-log|x|, V_s=|x|^-s for s>0; density rho and Gamma=beta*rho^(s/2). Neutralizing background is needed for highlighted s=0 and s=1.
primary_source.caution: The rendering's generated date is not a new arXiv version; use the version history. Numerical phase thresholds are not assumed rigorous. The source does not require two continuous transitions.

recent_primary_literature_check.finding: Li, Ding and Ma discuss energy/entropy in numerical two-dimensional melting models. Their inverse-power simulations use n=6,64 and a cut-and-shifted potential at r_c=2.5; this is not a rigorous thermodynamic hexatic-existence proof for the untruncated s=0 or s=1 Riesz jellium.
Mazars's primary numerical study of classical 1/r particles reports a hexatic regime and a weak first-order fluid/hexatic transition; this warns against adding two-continuous-transition hypotheses.
Muto and Aoki: molecular-dynamics positional and orientational diagnostics for the classical 2D electron system; numerical evidence, not a rigorous phase-existence theorem.
